[7.3.1](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x15-V7-Error-Logging.md#v73-log-protection-requirements)

> V7.3.1 Verify that the application appropriately encodes **user-supplied** data to prevent log injection. 

Do we actually need/want this "user-supplied" definition/condition/filter? If data does not come from classical end-user, but comes from some API for an example, and data contains new-lines, it still makes mess in log file.

It would be the same like recommend for "XSS" that only data from user need to be converted for output document, but in fact, you need to convert data from any source to have correct functionality.

Just removal of "user-supplied" it's also not good. But I need some language help here.

comments.body:
Well said.

I think the concept of user data or untrusted data can be dangerous and actually encourage bad practices. I say just drop “user supplied”.

--
Jim Manico
@Manicode

Proposal so far:
* 7.3.1 Verify that the application appropriately encodes data to prevent log injection.

Now I'm thinking about the "the application" part, isn't it too restrictive? It does not cover web server, database engine etc. Should we extend it to "the application and all it's components" or something like that?

I agree it does restrict and your suggestion works better. We could do something like 

Ensure all components that make up the application or functions,  appropriately encode data to prevent log injection.

"components that make up the application" I would interpret as framework, application, modules, plugins. I think it still may not cover web server, database engine etc part. But maybe it's just a lack of my skills in English.

Maybe just "all logging components"? And all separate logs should be detected by issue #892

It's not perfect but it's simple and clear and explains the point 
cleanly. I like it as is, I submit with respect.

- Jim

I personally like "7.3.1 Verify that the application appropriately encodes data to prevent log injection." and would like to see a PR on this.

Are we close to a PR?
